item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
580
ABPZ20 KNHC 240535
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Wed Sep 23 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located almost 100 miles offshore of southwestern Mexico, on
Hurricane Odalys, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of
Baja California, and on Tropical Storm Nolo, located a few hundred
miles south of the Big Island of Hawaii.

South of the Gulf of Tehuantepec:
An area of low pressure is expected to form in a couple of days to
the south of the Gulf of Tehuantepec. Afterwards, environmental
conditions should be favorable for gradual development, and a
tropical depression is likely to form early next week as the system
moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward, parallel to the
coast of southern and southwestern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
An area of low pressure could form about 1000 miles east-southeast
of the Hawaiian Islands over the weekend. Environmental conditions
could support some gradual development of this system thereafter as
it moves generally northeastward, remaining well east-southeast of
the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

&&

Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Nolo are issued under
WMO header WTPA32 PHFO and under AWIPS header TCPCP2.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Nolo are issued
under WMO header WTPA22 PHFO and under AWIPS header HFOTCMCP2.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Odalys was located 
near latitude 16.1 North, longitude 126.0 West. Odalys is moving 
toward the east-northeast near 8 mph (13 km/h). An 
east-northeastward motion at a slightly slower speed is expected for 
the next day or so, followed by a gradual turn toward the northeast 
and then north later this week.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 85 mph (140 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Additional strengthening is expected during the next day or 
so, followed by a weakening trend late this week.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 978 mb (28.88 inches).

item.title: Hurricane Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 17
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Thu Sep 24 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 240832
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Odalys Discussion Number  17
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
200 AM PDT Thu Sep 24 2026
 
The convective pattern of Odalys has changed little over the past 
several hours. A persistent area of deep convection with cloud-top 
temperatures near -80C remains concentrated near the inner core. 
Subjective Dvorak classification from TAFB, along with objective 
satellite intensity estimates, have held steady and generally range 
from 67 to 77 kt. Based on a blend of these data, the initial 
intensity is maintained at 75 kt for this advisory. In addition, 
recent scatterometer passes over the cyclone were helpful in 
refining the initial wind radii.

The initial motion is estimated to be east-northeastward, or 060/7 
kt. Odalys is currently being steered by the deep-layer flow between 
a mid- to upper-level trough located to its northwest and a 
mid-level ridge over northern Mexico. This steering pattern should 
maintain the east-northeastward heading for the next day or so, 
followed by a turn toward the northeast and eventually to the north 
at a slightly slower speed. Later in the forecast period, the track 
becomes highly uncertain due to a potential binary interaction with 
Hurricane Polo. Additionally, as Odalys weakens, model differences 
regarding the vertical depth of the cyclone, and exactly when it 
becomes steered by the shallow low-level flow. The updated NHC track 
forecast is very similar to the previous one and is in good 
agreement with the HCCA and GDMI aids.

Environmental conditions appear favorable enough to support slight 
intensification during the next day or so, with low to moderate 
vertical wind shear, warm sea surface temperatures, and abundant 
mid-level moisture. After that time, the cyclone will encounter a 
progressively less favorable environment characterized by increasing 
vertical wind shear, cooling sea surface temperatures, and mid-level 
dry air. This should induce a gradual, then more steady, weakening 
trend through the remainder of the forecast period. The NHC 
intensity forecast is very similar to the previous advisory and lies 
near the HCCA corrected consensus aid. Given the increasingly 
hostile environment, the system will struggle to maintain deep 
convection later in the period. Simulated infrared satellite imagery 
from the global models shows the cyclone becoming devoid of deep 
convection by 96 h, and the updated forecast now indicates the 
system will become post-tropical at that time.

item.description:

000

BULLETIN
Hurricane Polo Intermediate Advisory Number 15A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
600 AM CST Thu Sep 24 2026
 
...OUTER RAINBANDS OF EXTREMELY POWERFUL CATEGORY 5 POLO SPREADING
ACROSS SOUTHWESTERN MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 600 AM CST...1200 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.7N 104.0W
ABOUT 175 MI...280 KM WSW OF ZIHUATANEJO MEXICO
ABOUT 160 MI...260 KM S OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...160 MPH...260 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...924 MB...27.29 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Tecpan de Galeana to Manzanillo
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* West of Manzanillo to Playa Perula
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, in this case within 12 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere along the coast of southwestern Mexico and Baja
California Sur should monitor the progress of this system.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 600 AM CST (1200 UTC), the center of Hurricane Polo was located
near latitude 16.7 North, longitude 104.0 West. Polo is moving
toward the northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). A turn toward the
west-northwest is expected later today and Friday, followed by a
northwestward motion on Saturday. On the forecast track, the core of
Polo is expected to remain offshore of southwestern Mexico today
before moving farther out to sea.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 160 mph (260 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Polo is a category 5 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale.  Some near-term strengthening is possible, 
and Polo is expected to remain a powerful major hurricane for the 
next few days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125
miles (205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 924 mb (27.29 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are occurring along the coast of 
Mexico in the warning area and should persist today. Tropical storm 
conditions are possible within the watch area along the coast of 
Mexico later today.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals of 4 to 6
inches, with isolated maximum totals up to 8 inches across coastal
portions of the Mexican state of Guerrero through today. This
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides,
especially in areas of steep terrain. Rainfall of 2 to 4 inches is
possible in coastal portions of the Mexican states of Michoacan,
Colima, and Jalisco through today.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF: Swells generated by Polo will affect portions of the coast of
southwestern Mexico during the next couple of days. Swells will
spread northward along the coast of west-central Mexico and toward
Baja California Sur on Friday and into the weekend. These swells are
likely to cause life-threatening surf, rip currents, and coastal
flooding. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Thu Sep 24 2026 
719 
WTPZ42 KNHC 240833
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
300 AM CST Thu Sep 24 2026
 
Polo remains a powerful category 5 hurricane. Satellite images 
indicate that the cyclone is maintaining a clear, distinct, and 
circular eye surrounded by an intense and symmetric ring of deep 
convection. The initial intensity is held at 140 kt, near the upper 
end of the latest satellite intensity estimates. Although the core 
of the hurricane is about 50 to 100 n mi off the coast of 
southwestern Mexico, outer rainbands are spreading onshore and 
producing heavy rains. ASCAT data was helpful in adjusting the 
initial wind radii, confirming that tropical-storm-force winds are 
likely occurring along the coast of southwestern Mexico.
 
After jogging to the north last night, Polo appears to be on a more 
steady northwestward track now, with the initial motion estimated to 
be 310/8 kt. A building mid-level ridge over northern Mexico and the 
south-central U.S. should cause Polo to accelerate to the 
west-northwest over the next couple of days, taking the system 
away from southwestern Mexico during that time. Polo will likely 
reach the western periphery of the ridge over the weekend, and that 
should cause the hurricane to turn northward toward the Baja 
California Peninsula late this weekend and early next week. The 
NHC track forecast is similar to the previous one, and based on a 
blend of the HCCA, GDMI, and TVCN aids.
 
Fluctuations in strength seem likely over the next day or so while
Polo remains in favorable environmental conditions, and any changes
in strength during that time will likely be linked to internal
dynamics. However, gradual weakening is expected this weekend and
early next week due to an increase in vertical wind shear.
Regardless, Polo is forecast to be a major hurricane during the next
several days. This intensity forecast is similar to the previous 
one, and in best agreement with the HCCA guidance.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo will impact coastal portions
of southwest Mexico today. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
2. Tropical storm conditions are expected across portions
of the coast within the warning area from Tecpan de Galeana to
Manzanillo today.
 
3. Polo is forecast to approach the Baja California Peninsula early
next week as a hurricane. Interests there should closely monitor
the latest updates and ensure that they have their preparedness
plan in place.
